then.text: Our resident geneticist! Your pint of Eagle's DNA is on the house. It's ale. I just call it that.
You've seen the ceiling, now for the puzzle. DNA is a ladder, twisted. Each rung is two bases holding hands. A always pairs with T, and C always with G.
And the other strand of A-T-G-C reads...
T-A-C-G! Spot on. Each strand is a template for the other: unzip it and you can build the missing half. That's how life copies itself.

Crick and Watson built their model from metal plates and wire. Rosalind Franklin's Photo 51 from King's College London showed it was a helix. Crick, Watson and Maurice Wilkins got the Nobel Prize in 1962; Franklin had died in 1958, and it isn't given to the dead.
Here. A little gold helix from behind the bar. Pin it on whoever you like.

else.text: Not quite. Pair them up: A with T, T with A, G with C, C with G. Have a sip and try again.
No, A and T go together, like fish and chips. Have another go.

then.text: Go and look at the ceiling in the RAF bar first, at the back. Ask the regular. Then come and do my puzzle.

else.text: Welcome to the Eagle. Coaching inn since 1667. In 1953 two blokes from the Cavendish Lab down the road had their lunch here most days.
On 28 February, Francis Crick stood up at lunchtime and told the whole pub they had found the secret of life. Everyone assumed he'd had a few. He had found the shape of DNA.
I've a puzzle for you, if you're game. Fancy it?

then.text: Good. First, go and look at the ceiling in the RAF bar at the back. Ask the regular about it. Science starts with looking.

else.text: No rush. The secret of life will keep.

then.text: Look up. All those names and numbers, written on the ceiling in candle smoke and lighter flame and lipstick, by British and American airmen in the Second World War.
They came here from the airfields round Cambridge between missions. Some never came back. The pub kept the ceiling just as they left it.
Funny, isn't it. Two kinds of history in one pub. One's on the ceiling, one's on a plaque by the door. Go on, the barman's waiting with his puzzle.

else.text: Look up at the ceiling sometime. It's a war memorial written in smoke.

eagle_quizmaster.text: Quiz night at the Eagle. It's mostly science teams. Last week a team called Schrodinger's Cat both won and didn't.
Fancy a round? Five questions, no phones.

else.text: Fair enough. Come back when your neurons are warmed up.
